candidates.title: Draft invoice fields for bookkeeper review

demandEvidence.chore: Bookkeepers and small finance teams retype vendor invoice details from email into a spreadsheet.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Hi all, sharing a workflow I built for bookkeepers and small finance teams who still retype vendor invoices from email into a spreadsheet.

ease.reason: A beginner can test extraction from sample PDFs into a spreadsheet, but no attached implementation source documents this workflow.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: bookkeeping firms may pay for less invoice re-entry; this post does not establish customer payment or willingness to pay.

feasibility.reason: A four-week prototype can extract a few fields from synthetic invoice PDFs; vendor formats and accounting accuracy need human review.

autonomy.reason: PDF intake and draft field extraction could repeat, but a bookkeeper must verify values and resolve exceptions; no implementation reference is attached.

evidence.reason: The post explicitly describes bookkeepers retyping emailed vendor invoices into spreadsheets and shares a workflow, but gives limited evidence on frequency or outcomes.

candidates.reason: Assessed a narrow PDF-to-draft-fields experiment, but the equal-weight mean is 5.6, below the 6 threshold. No supplied implementation reference supports the mechanics. The second n8n assignment is the same post and chore.

rejected.title: Architecture Decision Record translations
rejected.reason: The only stated request is “constructive feedback” and help with translations; it names no concrete translation task, input, or bounded repeatable chore, so no AI service scope or candidate assessment is justified.

rejected.title: Euspell spelling reform software
rejected.reason: The source describes a spelling reform and its software, but gives no request for work or concrete chore; a demand-backed service duty would be invented.

rejected.title: Shopify stock-count recording
rejected.reason: The source explains staff recording shelf counts and reviewing differences, but this is an instructional description rather than a concrete unmet request. A proposed shop-inventory workflow would also share the specific online-retail customer with recent post 98b4f6281cc3de4ecdfa95f6 (customer overlap), so it is excluded.

rejected.title: Azure operations with CeruleanToolbox
rejected.reason: The source is only a product title and supplies no explicit chore, request, or demand context; inferring Azure operations duties from it would invent evidence.

rejected.title: Use a collected job-seeker contact list
rejected.reason: The post asks what to do with a collection of personal email addresses and names. A service using applicant contact data creates privacy risks, and the source establishes no safe bounded task; the personal data must not be processed.

rejected.title: Private Make support ticket
rejected.reason: The captured source contains only the generic prompt “What is the problem & what have you tried?” and no actual reported issue or chore.

rejected.title: Recurring Make billing charges
rejected.reason: The captured source contains only the generic prompt “What is the problem & what have you tried?” and no actual complaint details or task evidence; no billing duty can be inferred.

rejected.title: Capture checkout customer notes
rejected.reason: The request asks for a checkout feature where customers can add instructions, but implementation and repeated business work are unspecified; no supplied implementation reference supports a useful automated scope, so it is not scored as a candidate.

rejected.title: Duplicate invoice re-entry workflow
rejected.reason: This is a duplicate assignment of the same n8n post and invoice-retyping workflow as candidate https://community.n8n.io/t/323473; the second URL does not establish a distinct product or chore.

steps.message: Assessed the ten sealed discussion leads. The only concrete nonduplicate chore was invoice re-entry by bookkeepers; its proposed draft-extraction experiment scored below threshold, so this batch has no post.
